name: Translate a visible anomaly into a lower-level discriminating measurement
decision_structure: A robust high-level phenotype or pattern exists, but competing explanations remain observationally similar until a lower-level measurable property is compared.
rule: Convert the macroscopic anomaly into a measurement that can discriminate among plausible lower-level mechanisms, then test whether the measured difference tracks the phenotype as predicted.
operational_actions: Define the anomaly without embedding a preferred explanation.
Choose a measurement that separates at least two mechanisms.
Check whether intermediate/heterogeneous cases behave as the mechanism predicts.
boundary_conditions: The lower-level measurement must be linked to a plausible mechanism rather than selected post hoc.
Association at the molecular/measurement level is not automatically causal without additional design support.
failure_signals: The proposed measurement cannot distinguish rival mechanisms.
The measurement is selected only after seeing the desired pattern.
Cross-scale linkage relies on an untested causal bridge.

specificity.notes: Candidate heuristic. It has not yet been shown to be distinctive to Pauling rather than a generic mechanistic-research strategy.

notes: Candidate only; requires a contrastive episode, stronger process evidence, and v0.4 specificity testing.
